title: Membrane tension peaks at the small end, where abnormal eggs are irregular

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Membrane tension peaks at the small end, where abnormal eggs are irregular

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In conical eggs with spherical ends, the tension of the envelope is greatest at and near the small end, so that is where eggs are most likely to be distorted or to burst and where abnormal eggs most often show irregularities.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XV: On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: further, that the tension _T_ is greatest at and near the small end of the egg. It is here, in short, that the egg is most likely to be irregularly distorted or even to burst, and it is here that we most commonly find irregularities of shape in abnormal eggs.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XV, “On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures”; topic “Equation of the egg”. Scope: birds' eggs, especially pointed eggs and abnormal hen's eggs

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch15-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.57

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The predicted localization can be tested on existing images and production records, though ascertainment bias is serious. Direct confirmation of maximum membrane tension would require new mechanical measurements.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Code the spatial location of cracks, distortions and shape abnormalities on pointed eggs and compare their frequency near the small versus large end, while using shell mechanics to infer tension. Concentration at the small end supports the prediction; uniform or opposite localization refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Abnormality location tests the consequence, not tension directly.

Collections may exclude broken or abnormal eggs.

Damage after laying can mimic developmental failure.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The visible prediction is that irregularities and ruptures sit at the small end, where the membrane calculation puts the greatest tension. Normal egg profiles are richly measured, and the locations of abnormal features are not part of those releases; they appear as scattered notes and figures in the poultry and oology literature. Curvature can be checked now, while the defect prediction needs a compilation of abnormal eggs before it can be treated as a dataset test.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Locate distortions, thin shell, and rupture sites on pointed and abnormal eggs and test whether they concentrate at the narrow end. The observable prediction is supported by a significant small-end excess relative to area; a uniform distribution, or a large-end excess, would refute it. Peak tension itself remains an inference from curvature unless local stress is measured.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Collectors discard damaged eggs, so museum series under-represent the failures the claim is about.

Abnormal eggs and burst sites are not fields in the comparative shape datasets.
